title: OAuth Consent Phishing Targeting HR via Malicious App
description: An HR employee on HR-WS-022 clicked a phishing email requesting signature for employment policies and granted consent to a rogue OAuth application named "DocuShare" hosted at docs-secure-share.example. Attacker sign-in was observed from external IP 203.0.113.77. The malicious application requested high-privilege scopes including Mail.ReadWrite and User.Read.
root_cause: User granted OAuth consent to unverified third-party cloud app DocuShare
resolution: Revoked OAuth application consent organization-wide in Entra ID, revoked all active refresh tokens and user sessions, blocked docs-secure-share.example and IP 203.0.113.77 at firewall.
outcome: EFFECTIVE: Revoking application consent and invalidating all OAuth refresh tokens immediately terminated unauthorized access.

feedback.what_worked: Revoking OAuth app consent and active refresh tokens immediately stopped unauthorized mailbox access.

title: OAuth Consent Phishing Targeting Marketing Department
description: A marketing specialist on MKT-WS-019 was tricked into granting OAuth permissions to a fake analytics tool after a phishing lure. Authentication logs showed adversary access from 203.0.113.77. The SOC initially attempted a user password reset in Active Directory, but the attacker maintained persistent access through valid cloud refresh tokens.
root_cause: Illicit OAuth consent grant bypassed password controls via persistent refresh tokens
resolution: Password reset alone failed because OAuth tokens remained active. Remediation succeeded only after tenant-wide app consent revocation and revoking all OAuth refresh tokens and sessions.
outcome: NOT EFFECTIVE: Password reset alone was ineffective because OAuth refresh tokens remained valid. Revoking application consent and session tokens was required.

feedback.what_worked: Revoking OAuth app consent and active session tokens
feedback.what_failed: Password reset alone without revoking OAuth consent and refresh tokens
